messages:
marta: heads up — support ticket S-4721 from Acme reports p95/p99 spikes on /v1/generate starting ~03:20 UTC. They saw 99th go from ~220ms to ~1.3s. They say the application is timing out for interactive use. Any correlation with last night’s batching rollout? :rotating_light:

alex: oncall, looking. pulling dashboards now. link: https://dashboards.redwood/inference/p99?range=120m (internal)

sre-bot: alert: p99_latency("/v1/generate") > 1000ms for 10m — triggered at 03:23 UTC

alex: quick note — continuous-batching config was updated in last deploy (canary at 03:12) — default batch_timeout_ms bumped from 20 -> 120 in rollout config for a perf experiment. I’ll check rollout status.

priya: that’s likely. larger batch_timeout reduces GPU fragmentation but increases latency for light-traffic requests. if low qps routes are waiting to fill batches, tail spikes.

alex: confirmed — rollout manager shows 100% for cluster-prod-a at 03:15. commit: 8f1b3e5 — changed continuous-batching.default_max_wait_ms = 120.

marta: sigh. customer escalated and is close to hitting SLA. recommend immediate mitigation: revert or hotfix route for Acme to low-wait profile.

jen: can we do a targeted override for the route? we have per-route batching profiles.

alex: yes. running command now to set per-route override for Acme route id "route-acme-19" to max_wait_ms=20 and max_batch_size=16.

alex: reply from rictl: 
```
$ rictl config update --route route-acme-19 --set continuous_batching.max_wait_ms=20 --set continuous_batching.max_batch_size=16
update started: cfg-3372
applied to route-acme-19 on cluster-prod-a
```

support-bot: support S-4721: patch applied. customer notified.

marta: prod metrics — did p99 drop for that route?

alex: checking per-route latency. short window: before patch p99=1.25s; after ~1.25 -> 320ms within 4 minutes for route-acme-19. global p99 still elevated because other routes + background traffic.

priya: good quick mitigation. we should also roll back the global change — it’s too aggressive. I’ll run rollback to default 20ms for continuous-batching across clusters.

alex: are there any other customers hitting timeouts? support shows three other tickets (S-4723, S-4724, S-4726) flagged with similar symptoms. I’ll list all routes impacted via query: 
```
# prometheus-ish pseudo
topk(20, increase(requests_total{route=~".*"}[15m]) > 0) by (route)
queue_time_p99{route=~".*"} > 500
```

alex: found 7 routes with queue_time_p99 > 500ms, mostly low qps streaming routes.

jen: we need a safe rollback plan. can we do a config rollback via deploy-tool and gradually reintroduce the experiment?

priya: plan: 1) rollback global default to previous 20ms 2) leave per-route overrides for customers who benefit from higher batching (batch-heavy routes) 3) add a canary guard that prevents default_max_wait_ms > 50ms unless explicitly approved for a cohort.

marta: agree. timeline? customer-facing communication?

alex: rolling global rollback now (cluster-prod-a then prod-b). command: 
```
$ rictl config update --global --set continuous_batching.default_max_wait_ms=20 --force
apply started: cfg-rollback-3373
```

sre-bot: deploy event: cfg-rollback-3373 applied to cluster-prod-a at 03:48 UTC

alex: prod-b queued, will be done by 03:55.

marta: support sent templated update to Acme and affected customers: we’re reverting an experimental batching change, we expect latency to normalize in <10min after each cluster rollback.

support-bot: S-4721 updated: customer acknowledged.

priya: root cause summary to add later: the experiment increased default wait to 120ms to improve throughput for heavy batchers, but for low-QPS interactive routes the scheduler ends up waiting much longer to fill batches, so request queue time dominates token generation time. impact concentrated on routes without per-route override.

alex: repro steps for eng-runtime to reproduce locally and validate fix (put in thread for runbook):
1) start local runtime with continuous-batching enabled and defaults: 
```
# start local runtime with modified config
RUNTIME_CONFIG="continuous_batching.default_max_wait_ms=120
continuous_batching.default_max_batch_size=128" make run-local
```
2) run low QPS synthetic workload: single-connections with Poisson arrivals ~0.5 rps per route: 
```
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' &
  sleep 2
done
```
3) measure request latency and query internal batcher metrics at /metrics: queue_time_ms_bucket, batch_fill_ms, batch_size_histogram.

4) confirm p95/p99 queue_time increase when default_max_wait_ms >= 100ms and growth is concentrated on small routes.

jen: add follow-ups:
- Add a new alert: continuous_batching.queue_time_p99_global > 250ms for 5m (pager) — owner: jen — ETA: 24h
- Add per-route queue_time metrics to console and expose route-level default_batch_profile (low_latency/high_throughput) — owner: priya — ETA: 5d
- Add experiment guardrail: config change that increases global default_max_wait_ms > 50 requires PR with perf runbook and canary approval — owner: marta — ETA: 3d

marta: also add a mitigation to runtime: if queue_time > threshold for N requests, dynamically reduce max_wait_ms for that route until it stabilizes. file an RFC.

alex: documenting immediate postmortem notes and will open postmortem ticket PM-129. linking logs and traces in the incident doc.

marta: thanks all — good triage and quick per-route fix. keep thread updated if anything re-escalates. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: incident closed for now: latency regression mitigated for impacted routes. postmortem PM-129 created.
